project: Exactly-Once Effects for Re-Planning LLM Agents: A Reduction, a Retention Hazard, and an Evidence Contract
previous_title: Intent Identity and Exactly-Once Effects for Non-Deterministic LLM Agents
status: executed development research; independent re-implementation; not submitted
main_findings: v0.2 null result reproduced exactly by an independent implementation; a ledger-consulting strong reference R+ ties the verifier V in effects and in sink calls.

Under finite idempotency retention (documented: Stripe >= 24 h, SQS FIFO 5 min), every same-key-retry policy (R, R+, V) duplicates in all 149,217 lost-acknowledgement cases; the retention-aware controller duplicates in none.
Completion after the window depends on an evidence contract: retention-aware recovery completes 20/20 lost-ack runtime trials with a lookup endpoint and 0/20 without (safe, unresolved).

Ternary per-obligation state is sufficient for the safe fresh-dispatch frontier but not for reconciliation cost; the batch processing class of a lost request changes exact optimal probe cost from n to 1 (atomic), ~log2(n+1) (prefix), or the exact-k closed form.
Reservation-resolved three-worker races never exercise sink deduplication (0 of 96 sink calls), so they are not evidence about the sink contract.
